change.title: pr-36882-flat
change.description: Add rolling-updates feature flag and compatibility framework
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Operator guide says the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but no operator code checks it
findings.body: The CAUTION says the Operator "will fail" when the `rolling-updates` feature is off. Nothing in the operator reads that feature. `UpgradeLogicFactory.create` (operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/upgrade/UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35-43) picks the upgrade logic from `spec.update.strategy` alone, and nothing under `operator/src/main/.../upgrade` mentions features. `UpgradeTest` itself deploys the default (`<not set>`) strategy without the feature (UpgradeTest.java:105-107) and expects it to succeed. The `features.enabled` entry in the CR only becomes a `--features` server option (KeycloakDistConfigurator.java:121-124). Either say what actually breaks (for example, that later releases will require it), or limit the caution to setting `spec.update.strategy`.

findings.title: Template's hard-coded `--features=rolling-updates` replaces the user's own feature list
findings.body: The macro adds a fixed `--features=rolling-updates` to every `update-compatibility` example. A CLI option takes priority over `KC_FEATURES` and `keycloak.conf`, so a user who keeps features such as `token-exchange` in config and copies this command runs `metadata`/`check` with only `rolling-updates` enabled. That contradicts the guide's own warning (update-compatibility.adoc:70-75, 85-91) to pass the exact configuration, or the metadata will be wrong. It can also make `validateConfig()` reject options that need one of the dropped features. Suggest telling users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing `--features` value instead of hard-coding it into the template.

findings.title: Enabling the feature in the test CR exercises nothing in the operator
findings.body: The feature is enabled only when a strategy is set (the null case returns at line 106). The operator never checks it (UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35-43), so this line only adds `--features=rolling-updates` to the server and the test does not cover any feature-gated behaviour. If the operator is meant to require the feature, as the guide says, that check and a negative test are missing. If not, this setup and the Dockerfile change (`operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image:5`) can go.

findings.title: Exit code 4 changes meaning from 'recreate required' to 'feature disabled'
findings.body: Before this change, `check` exited with 4 when a recreate was needed. It now exits with 3, and 4 means the feature is disabled. This matches the documented table (update-compatibility.adoc:128-134), which already listed 3. Scripts written against the old binary's 4 will now read a recreate result (3) as an unknown code. The command is preview, so this is acceptable; a release note would help. No test in this PR checks the exit code of either the disabled path or the incompatible path.

contracts.action: update-compatibility metadata/check refuse to run unless Profile feature ROLLING_UPDATES is enabled
contracts.equivalent_path: Other CLI paths read the feature profile only after Picocli sets it up; update-compatibility skips the rebuild check (Picocli.java:251-259), so the profile comes from sanitizeDisabledMappers on the non-rebuild path
contracts.before_after: Picocli.parseAndRun calls PropertyMappers.sanitizeDisabledMappers() before cmd.execute (Picocli.java:127-129), and that calls Environment.getCurrentOrCreateFeatureProfile() (PropertyMappers.java:301-306), so Profile.CURRENT is set before run() calls Profile.isFeatureEnabled (Profile.java:408-410). The new check runs before printPreviewWarning/validateConfig, like the existing flow.
contracts.visible_effect: Prints 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled.' to stderr (AbstractUpdatesCommand.java:83-85), then picocli.exit(4) calls System.exit(4) outside test launch mode (Picocli.java:203-208). The guide documents this code at update-compatibility.adoc:132-134.
contracts.failure_mode: In test launch mode exit() does not call System.exit; the explicit `return` stops execution, so no metadata is written and no check runs.

contracts.action: UpgradeTest enables rolling-updates through the CR FeatureSpec when an update strategy is set
contracts.equivalent_path: KeycloakDistConfigurator.configureFeatures maps FeatureSpec.enabledFeatures to the server's `features` option
contracts.before_after: The operator chooses the upgrade logic from UpdateSpec.strategy only (UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35-43); the feature is passed to the server but the operator never reads it.
contracts.visible_effect: No change in operator behaviour; the server gets --features=rolling-updates.

summary: The PR adds a preview `rolling-updates` feature. Without it, the `update-compatibility metadata` and `check` commands print an error and exit with the new code 4; the "recreate required" result moves from code 4 to 3, which matches the existing docs. The CLI gating is correct: the feature profile is set up in `Picocli.parseAndRun` (via `sanitizeDisabledMappers`) before `run()` reads it. Three doc/test issues are at "consider" level. First, the operator guide says the Operator fails without the feature, but no operator code checks it; upgrade logic depends only on `spec.update.strategy`. Second, the docs template hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates`, which replaces a user's own feature list and works against the guide's "pass your exact configuration" warning. Third, the change to `UpgradeTest` enables a feature the operator never reads, so it tests nothing. One info note: scripts that relied on the old exit code 4 will now see 3 for a recreate result, and no test asserts either exit code.
